claim: find_safe_compaction_split orphans trailing ToolMessages when a turn ends with multiple parallel tool results, producing an invalid message history that LLM providers reject.
evidence: In Agent-Core/agent_core/context_manager.py:583-584, the loop advances candidate while candidate < n - 1 and isinstance(messages[candidate], ToolMessage), stopping at candidate = n - 1 when messages[n - 1] is a ToolMessage. Lines 588-593 then check only whether messages[candidate - 1] is an AIMessage; when an AIMessage invoked >= 2 tools in parallel, messages[candidate - 1] is another ToolMessage, so candidate stays at n - 1 and is returned at line 597. compact_conversation_history (lines 686-691) therefore compacts the AIMessage and earlier ToolMessages while leaving messages[n - 1] as an orphaned ToolMessage.
runtimeTrigger: During a single-turn or multi-tool run where context usage hits >= 80% after an AIMessage with 2+ parallel tool_calls (e.g., [HumanMessage, AIMessage(tc1, tc2), ToolMessage(tc1), ToolMessage(tc2)]), find_safe_compaction_split computes candidate=2, advances to 3, skips the line 588 check because messages[2] is a ToolMessage, and returns 3. The next LLM call sends [ToolMessage(tc2)] without its preceding AIMessage(tool_calls), failing with provider HTTP 400 invalid tool message sequence.

claim: list_provider_models and probe_model_connectivity perform SSRF-prone HTTP requests with follow_redirects=True to arbitrary base_url values while attaching server-side provider API keys.
evidence: Agent-Core/agent_core/models.py:1233-1266 accepts an arbitrary base_url (checking only startswith(('http://','https://')) in list_provider_models and omitting scheme checks in probe_model_connectivity at line 1339), resolves server-side API keys from os.environ via _resolve_api_key when api_key is omitted, attaches them via _build_provider_headers, and opens httpx.AsyncClient(follow_redirects=True) without blocking private/loopback/metadata IP ranges or restricting hostnames.
runtimeTrigger: Calling Agent-Core POST /config/models or POST /config/probe (or via Express /api/settings/models and /api/settings/probe) with a known provider name (e.g., openai), an omitted api_key, and a custom base_url pointing to an external collector or internal/metadata service causes Agent-Core to transmit the configured server-side API key to that host or probe internal network services.
